items.title: Colour validator used CSS.supports, the wrong authority
items.detail: Color.fromJson returns null WITHOUT throwing for red / hsl(...) / rgb(0 0 0 / 50%) / RGBA(...), all of which CSS.supports accepts. So the engine never rejected them, lap 1's apply-before-persist gate never fired, the null was stored, and the renderer dereferenced null.rgba inside a queued frame - outside that try/catch. Replaced with the engine's own grammar (3/6/8-digit hex + lowercase rgb()/rgba()); verified to agree with Color.fromJson on all 17 cases tested.

items.title: Font family list was a script-injection sink
items.detail: isFontShorthand deliberately did not validate the family list. SvgCanvas builds `<text ... style='... font:${...}'>` as a SINGLE-quoted attribute and assigns it as markup (alphaTab.core.mjs:49768), so an apostrophe closes the attribute. Confirmed `12px <image onerror=...>` passed the validator. A stored value re-arms on every visit. Now refuses ' < > ; keeps " so `12px "Times New Roman"` still works.

open_findings.title: requestNotation has no guard against two overlapping file opens
open_findings.whats_wrong: Neither the file input nor the drop zone disables while an open is in flight, and `opening` is not set until after an early await - so two opens race and the last to resolve silently wins.

open_findings.title: Rapid double-toggle of two tracks' visibility drops the first toggle
open_findings.whats_wrong: applyRendered computes its replacement set from drawnIndexes, which only updates on the async renderFinished event, so a second toggle before that fires silently discards the first.

open_findings.title: The CSS canary matches by substring, so a longer utility satisfies a prefix entry

open_findings.note: Adversarial explicitly CLEARED the self-satisfaction question the brief asked: globals.css still excludes web/scripts/**, so naming a utility there does not make Tailwind generate it.

open_findings.title: The Transpose notation row seeds at 0 over a file's own transposition
open_findings.whats_wrong: Three modules disagree about what 0 means: the engine preserves a file-carried transposition, lap 1's densify loop reads it back specifically to avoid losing it, but toMixerTrack still seeds the row at 0. So the slider reads at rest while the engine holds +2, and returning it to 0 writes a literal 0 - which erases the file's value, irrecoverably without reopening.

decided.title: Mixer size-exemption keys on the ROW, so all four mixer sliders lose the 44px verdict
decided.whats_wrong: sizeExempt matches el.closest('[data-slot="track-row"], [data-slot="master-row"]'), so every slider inside a mixer row - per-track volume, Transpose audio, Transpose notation, Master volume - is exempt from the size check, not just the deliberate 34px icon buttons the exemption is justified for. A mixer rail painted 0px wide is exactly the NH-315 failure this function exists to catch, and the gate would return [] and go green.
decided.note: The over-broad scope is PRE-EXISTING (the original `if (el.closest(...)) return false;` had the same reach); lap 1 narrowed it to the size verdict but did not narrow WHICH elements it covers.
decided.proposed_fix: AND the mixer half with el.matches('button, [role="button"]'). The sliders are already h-11 w-full, so the lane stays green.

triage.how: sizeExempt now ANDs the mixer half with el.matches('button, [role="button"]'), so the four mixer sliders keep the 44px verdict. Justifying comment rewritten to say element-not-ancestry.

decided.title: The restore path gates enums and numbers but not the 13 text rows
decided.whats_wrong: loadStoredSettings repairs enum names (dropUnknownOptions) and numeric ranges (clampToBounds) but has no equivalent for the twelve font rows and the colour row - even though each already owns a validator in settings-schema.ts that simply is not exported or reused. fillFromJson has no per-key try/catch, so one bad stored font or colour silently aborts the ENTIRE restore, including unrelated notation/player groups, swallowed by the bare catch in PlayerShell and with reset staying false so no toast fires and no repair write happens.
decided.note: This is the restore-side twin of the write-side holes lap 1 closed. Reliability reached the same root cause from the other direction, adding that the stale field then rides along on every later edit and makes unrelated valid edits fail too.
decided.proposed_fix: Export the two validators as SETTING_TEXT_VALIDATORS and add a dropInvalidText pass mirroring dropUnknownOptions, folding into the same reset flag.

triage.how: SETTING_TEXT_VALIDATORS exported from settings-schema (the rows' OWN isCssColor/isFontShorthand, not copies); dropInvalidText added to settings-storage mirroring dropUnknownOptions, folded into the same reset flag; PlayerShell passes it. Two drift tests assert the map equals every text row's validate BY IDENTITY, in both directions. Four new storage cases.

decided.title: MIDI-apply rows reload the MIDI on every keystroke, stopping and rewinding playback per digit
decided.whats_wrong: SettingRow's number control reports on every keystroke (commit only gates CLAMPING, not whether onChange fires). All fourteen apply:'midi' rows are kind:'number'. pushSettings' 'render' branch is coalesced through requestAnimationFrame for exactly this reason; the 'midi' branch is not - so typing a three-digit value calls loadMidiForScore three times, and that call stops and rewinds the player. Each reload also re-fires TracksPopover's playerReady, re-flooding the synth worker with a full mixer resync per digit.
decided.note: PRE-EXISTING (not introduced by lap 1), and it contradicts the PR's stated invariant that neither popover blocks playback.
decided.proposed_fix: Coalesce the 'midi' branch the way 'render' already is, with its OWN flag so the two coalesce independently.

triage.decision: Apply after a spike (maintainer required proof first)
triage.how: 'midi' branch now goes through queueMidi, coalesced per frame with its own flag.
triage.spike_findings: THEORY CONFIRMED, with two corrections to the finding. (1) The finding said all FOURTEEN apply:'midi' rows are kind:'number'; it is THIRTEEN — player.playTripletFeel is a toggle and never had the problem. (2) The finding said typing '100' reloads three times; driving the real SettingRow measured FOUR — reports [1, 10, 100] while typing plus 100 again on blur. Engine side verified in the installed alphaTab 1.8.4: AlphaSynth.loadMidiFile does this.stop() then this.tickPosition = 0. Measured through applySettingsJson: 4 loadMidiForScore calls before, 1 after; the render path measured 1 for the same input, confirming the mechanism is the existing house pattern.

decided.title: renderQueued is module-level, so it ignores which api instance queued it
decided.whats_wrong: useAlphaTab recreates the api whenever its [engine] effect re-runs, which next.config.ts's Strict Mode deliberately exercises. A render queued for a stale instance suppresses a fresh instance's request in the same frame, and the stale callback calls .render() on a destroyed api. The test file's own afterEach comment already treats this flag as leaked module state.

triage.decision: Apply — maintainer chose to fold in rather than defer
triage.how: Both queues moved from module-global booleans to a WeakMap keyed by AlphaTabApi instance, so a frame queued for a destroyed api can no longer suppress a fresh one. Handle compared against undefined, not truthiness, because 0 is a valid frame handle.

decided.title: A queued render fires on a destroyed AlphaTabApi after unmount
decided.whats_wrong: The requestAnimationFrame handle is discarded, and AlphaTabApiBase.render() has NO _isDestroyed guard (unlike changeTrackVolume/Mute/Solo and its other siblings), so the deferred call runs against a destroyed renderer from a detached callback nothing in the tree can catch. The window widens on a backgrounded tab, where rAF is throttled.
decided.proposed_fix: Keep the frame handle and export a cancel, called from useAlphaTab's effect cleanup beside created.destroy().

triage.decision: Apply — maintainer chose to fold in rather than defer
triage.how: Frame handles are kept and cancelQueuedFrames(api) is exported; useAlphaTab's effect cleanup calls it immediately before created.destroy(). Mutation-checked: reinstating truthiness fails 3 tests, removing the cancel fails 1, collapsing per-instance keying to a global fails 2.

decided.title: applySetting's engine-reject path is untested at any level
decided.whats_wrong: The apply-before-persist ordering is lap 1's headline guarantee and nothing proves it: no test forces a rejection and asserts the toast fires AND nothing was stored.
decided.note: Testing flagged this manual/human because it is coupled to React state inside a component-local useCallback; the suggested route is extracting the ordering into a helper testable against a fake api, as live-settings.ts already is.

triage.decision: Apply — maintainer chose the extract-a-helper route over an e2e test
triage.how: Ordering extracted as applyThenPersist in live-settings.ts; PlayerShell passes the toast and a persist closure carrying both the state write and the storage write. Three cases: accepts/persists, rejects/persists NOTHING, and no-engine-yet. Mutation-checked: moving persist() above the engine call fails the rejection case.
triage.note: The e2e route was rejected for a reason worth keeping: O2's field-level validators now refuse a bad font or colour BEFORE the engine sees it, so this gate is a second line of defence and is hard to reach by typing. Closing the field hole is what made the e2e route weak.

decided.title: Lap 1's useMemo was half the fix - all 90 rows still rebuild every frame
decided.whats_wrong: Memoising buildSettingGroups stops the descriptor tree rebuilding, but SettingsPopover itself is not memoised, so its body - the 90-row map, valueOf, and a fresh closure per row - still runs on every animation frame during playback. apiValues is a fresh object literal built inline in PlayerShell on every render, which would defeat a shallow memo comparison even if one were added.
decided.proposed_fix: useMemo apiValues in PlayerShell, then wrap SettingsPopover in memo(). The other props are already reference-stable.

triage.decision: Apply after a spike (maintainer doubted the premise and asked for measurement)
triage.how: apiValues memoised in PlayerShell; SettingsPopover wrapped in memo(). Permanent regression test at web/app/play/SettingsPopover.test.tsx.
triage.spike_findings: THEORY CONFIRMED. The maintainer's challenge was whether the on-blur commit made this moot; it does not — the two are independent. Blur governs when a PERSON changes a value; O7 is about the PLAYER re-rendering the popover while the song runs. Measured by rendering the real popover with the real engine namespace and counting readSettingValue (one call per settings-sourced row): with memo() but apiValues still a fresh literal, 71 rows re-read PER FRAME with the popover CLOSED; with memo() plus a stable apiValues, 0. So both halves are needed and each is useless alone. Closed is not idle because the row map sits in JSX children, evaluated when the element is created rather than when the popover opens. The finding's claim that the other props are already reference-stable was VERIFIED, not assumed: applySetting:572, applyApiValue:540 and runAction:605 are all useCallback-wrapped, settings and api are state, mixUnavailable is a module constant or undefined.
triage.spike_process_note: The first run of this spike reported 0 rebuilds per frame, which would have DISPROVEN the finding. It was a dead harness: the clicks were not wrapped in act(), so the parent never re-rendered. Caught by asserting the tick counter had advanced before reading anything into the zero. The permanent test keeps that assertion.

decided.title: Text rows validate the trimmed draft but commit the untrimmed one
decided.whats_wrong: Both validators judge draft.trim(); commitText reports textDraft verbatim. Neither AlphaTab parser trims, so a value with surrounding whitespace passes the gate and can still be rejected by the engine.

triage.scenario: You paste a colour copied from somewhere else into Secondary voices. Copying almost always brings a space with it. The field accepts it silently, so it looks applied — then the next redraw throws where nothing can catch it, and the bad value is saved, so it happens again on every visit.
triage.how: commitText now reports textDraft.trim(). Mutation-checked: restoring the raw commit fails the new case.
triage.spike: SEVERITY UPGRADED P2 -> P1, and the finding's claim CORRECTED. Measured against alphaTab 1.8.4: ' #2DD4BF', '#2DD4BF ', '  #2DD4BF  ' and ' rgba(0,0,0,0.5)' all pass the field validator (it trims) and all return null from Color.fromJson WITHOUT throwing, because fromJson tests startsWith('#')/startsWith('rgb') on the RAW string. That defeats the apply-before-persist gate, which only fires on a throw, so the null is stored and the renderer dereferences null.rgba a frame later. HOWEVER the finding said 'neither AlphaTab parser trims' — that is WRONG. Font.fromJson was measured on ' 12px serif', '12px serif ' and '  12px serif ' and parsed all three correctly (serif @12). Only the colour row breaks; the twelve font rows were never at risk.

decided.title: SettingRow's local draft never reconciles an externally-pushed value
decided.whats_wrong: There is a real dual-editor case: playbackSpeed is written by both the header's TempoControl and the Settings popover's speed row.

triage.scenario: The finding implies: you are dragging the Playback speed slider and the speed changes from somewhere else mid-drag, so your release overwrites it. Leo raised the sharpest version — a song with tempo changes, where the BPM pill moves on its own during playback.
triage.spike: NOT REACHABLE, verified two ways. (1) PlayerShell:507 names applySpeed the ONLY writer of api.playbackSpeed, and it has exactly two callers — the settings row (:555) and the header tempo control (:866). No keyboard shortcut, timer or effect writes it. (2) Leo's tempo-change case: PlayerShell:417 does setScoreTempo(next.originalTempo) live during playback, but that writes scoreTempo, NEVER speed. The settings row is a pure percentage (Math.round(speed*1000)/10) and never reads scoreTempo, so which bar is playing cannot move it. The header's BPM pill DOES divide by the base tempo and therefore does need protection — and already has it: TempoControl freezes `editBase` at the start of an edit and uses `base = editBase ?? scoreTempo`, so a mid-drag tempo change cannot compound.
triage.why_dropped: The patch (useEffect clearing draft on value change) guards nothing reachable and would cost a real regression: any future external write would yank the slider out from under an in-flight drag.

decided.proposed_fix: Return the scanned count too and assert a floor.

triage.how: expectHitAreas takes a measured floor {controls, sliders}. Sliders are counted separately because a total cannot see one CATEGORY vanish: the seek rail is 1 control out of 13 on /play.

triage.spike: MUTATION-VERIFIED end to end. Ran the real suite: 9 passed. Renamed '[data-slot="slider-control"]' to a bogus value: 8 of 9 FAILED naming the stale selector (the 9th is landing, which legitimately has 0 sliders). Restored: 9 passed. Before this change that same rename passed all nine silently.

Answered with evidence: data-testid IS an existing convention here (9 production files), but it would relocate the coupling rather than remove it, cannot be applied to the third-party '[data-sonner-toast]' selector at all, and only lowers the CHANCE of a silent break where the floor DETECTS one. He chose the per-selector slider floor instead of adding a testid.

decided.title: settleToasts hard-fails on a toast that is dismissing, and misses one about to land
decided.whats_wrong: It pins .first() and waits for opacity '1'. A toast mid-dismiss moves the other way and then detaches, so the poll runs to the 5s deadline and fails the test - and layout.tsx sets duration={5000}, so that window is routine. Races adds the mirror problem: a single count() snapshot returns immediately in the gap before a triggering toast reaches the DOM.
decided.note: This is lap 1's own addition, introduced to stop the new position check racing a slide-in.
decided.proposed_fix: Poll page.evaluate over ALL toasts with .every(), rather than pinning .first() and waiting for a single opacity value.

triage.scenario: A test that raised a toast earlier fails five seconds later for no visible reason. The helper meant to wait for toasts to stop animating pinned the FIRST toast and waited for it to become fully opaque — but a toast that is dismissing animates the other way, so the wait never succeeds and takes the test down with it.
triage.how: Polls every toast for either settled state ('1' or '0') instead of pinning .first() and demanding '1'. An empty list settles immediately, preserving the old early return.
triage.spike: Verified by running the a11y suite locally: 9 passed before and after.

decided.title: The scroll-ancestor reprieve never checks the container is actually visible
decided.whats_wrong: Lap 1's new ancestor check tests EDGES, not extent. A collapsed scroll box sits inside every edge, its children are still laid out, and contentTop+height<=scrollHeight holds by construction - so everything inside passes. TracksPopover's viewport max-height is a runtime calc(), which is a reachable trigger.

triage.scenario: The Tracks popover sizes its list at runtime. If that calculation ever collapses the box to zero height, every mixer row inside is invisible — but the gate hands those controls a 'they are in a scroll container, just below the fold' pass and never checks whether they are reachable at all. A popover full of unreachable controls goes green.
triage.how: Added `if (ar.width <= 0 || ar.height <= 0) return true;` before the edge checks.
triage.spike: (UNTESTED as to the trigger) — a collapsed container was not reproduced; the reviewer rated confidence 50 and the runtime calc() is plausible but unobserved. The change itself IS verified as safe: strictly a tightening, and the 9 real cases still pass.

decided.title: The nosemgrep comment misstates what Object.hasOwn blocks
decided.whats_wrong: The guards DO hold - security could not pollute Object.prototype by any path shape - but for a reason the code does not state: computed keys and object spread use CreateDataProperty, which never runs the __proto__ setter. The stated reason is checkably false, since Object.hasOwn(JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{}}'), '__proto__') is true. A suppression carrying a wrong justification is the finding.

triage.decision: Apply — AUTO-RESOLVED (ambiguity-only: a wrong comment, no behaviour change)
triage.scenario: Nothing goes wrong for a person using the app. The next developer to audit the security suppression reads its justification, finds it false, and has to re-derive from scratch whether the code is safe at all.
triage.spike: CONFIRMED the comment is wrong AND the code is safe. Object.hasOwn(JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{}}'), '__proto__') returns TRUE, so hasOwn does not rule out '__proto__' as claimed. But neither the computed-key assignment nor the object spread polluted Object.prototype when run — because a computed key uses CreateDataProperty, which never invokes the '__proto__' setter. Both comments now state the true reason; the write path also warns off the two shapes that WOULD invoke it.

decided.title: The scroll-ancestor walk climbs past overflow:hidden clippers
decided.whats_wrong: Only auto/scroll match, so a permanent clipper is skipped; and an overflow-x-hidden ancestor computes overflow-y:auto and is mis-adopted as a scroller - a rule Table.tsx already documents.

triage.decision: Drop — maintainer chose to discard entirely, nothing to reproduce
triage.scenario: The finding implies a control is cut off and unreachable, but the test picks the wrong parent box when deciding whether it is merely scrolled out of view, and excuses it.
triage.spike: CSS RULE REAL, TRIGGER ABSENT. Verified in a browser that `overflow-x: hidden` makes overflow-y compute to `auto` — even when overflow-y:visible is written explicitly — so a purely horizontal clipper would be adopted as a vertical scroller. But the tree was checked: the only permanent clipper above these controls is PlayerShell's `<main className="flex h-dvh flex-col overflow-hidden">`, whose box IS the viewport, so the existing window check already covers it; and the only overflow-x-hidden in the design system (DropdownMenu) explicitly pairs overflow-y-auto, so adopting it is correct. Nothing in Tracks or Settings triggers either hole.
triage.why_dropped: The maintainer asked how to reproduce it and there is no answer — it is a trap for future code, not a present defect. He chose to discard rather than ticket.

decided.title: The gate checks horizontal clipping against the window, not the scroll box

triage.decision: Apply — AUTO-RESOLVED under the standing test-fix instruction, after the spike made the approach certain
triage.scenario: On a phone, a control sits completely off the right of the screen with no way to scroll to it — and the test that exists to catch exactly that passes, because the overflow pushing the control away also inflated the width the test compares against.
triage.spike: MEASURED IN A BROWSER, and it reframed the finding. The artifact called this 'checked against the window, not the scroll box'; the sharper truth is that innerWidth ITSELF lies. On a 375px phone with the Tracks popover open: visualViewport.width 375, innerWidth 517, documentElement.scrollWidth 517. The fix uses visualViewport.width with an innerWidth fallback. The risk worth checking was the OPPOSITE direction — visualViewport excludes a scrollbar where innerWidth includes it, which could newly fail edge controls — so all nine cases were run: 9 passed, nothing moved.
